unit: EUR bn nominal (years); EUR bn at 2019-2021 prices (base); index 2019-2021 = 1 (pidx)
layer: years, base and pidx are the final series as site/data.json carries them (after re-exports, residual, freight and the Brunei refinery step), produced by running the current builder with the input changes in each entry's 'inputs'. The builder should take the 'inputs' (customs-level and parameter changes), not the final values, so nothing is applied twice.
how_to_apply: Each entry's 'inputs' says which research file value it replaces. A copy of the builder run with these inputs reproduces every 'years'/'base'/'pidx' here (scratch: r7/actuals/scripts/patch.py). Series not listed are unchanged.

checked_overlaps.narrow.json: KAZ/KGZ/MNG to_rus and KAZ from_rus: only the low/high bands of narrow.json's trade_layer (and trade_full's own-report years) change; centrals are kept. ARM to_rus: narrow.json's trade_layer is kept; the change is in reexports.json's gold pass-through. BRN: narrow.json's values were already superseded by laundered_r6.json (apply_brunei_r6); this file replaces laundered_r6's residual. TJK, YEM, SYR are not in narrow.json.
checked_overlaps.laundered_r6.json: BRN: replaces refiner.option_b_residual_kept_by_brunei_eur_bn (to_rus and its 2021 base). The deduction passed to fuel buyers (deduct_exported_crude_value_eur_bn) and the buyers' laundered-oil series are NOT changed; only the residual's range is recomputed with one Russian crude share applied to both intake and deduction.
checked_overlaps.reexports.json: ARM: replaces hubs.ARM.reexports_from_RUS (gold and diamonds passed on). The extra gold passed on goes to the buyers through destination_shares as now: UAE +0.06 to +0.18, China +0.02 to +0.04, Hong Kong +0.01 to +0.03 EUR bn a year (central). No other hub changed. Checked: Armenia's HS 71 exports exceed its HS 71 imports from all origins in every year 2019-2025, so the pass-through is real, not a double count with Armenia's own sales.
checked_overlaps.nonreport.json: TJK imports_from_RUS 2023-2026 and YEM/SYR 2019-2021 bands replaced; paid shares unchanged.
checked_overlaps.windfall: BLR: the new crude index raises Belarus's fuel windfall by EUR 0.27-0.61bn a year (central), because it includes the end of the Russian export duty (tax manoeuvre). See notes: part of that is not a war effect.

to_rus.reasoning: The width came from the Russian gold Armenia passes on, ranged 64-95% of Armstat's own HS 71 imports from Russia. Armstat: HS 71 imports from Russia USD 0.40bn (2022), 2.26 (2023), 6.99 (2024), 2.39bn (2025); Armenia's HS 71 exports exceed its HS 71 imports from all origins every year 2019-2025 (2024: 8.05 vs 7.37bn), so 95-100% (central 98%) is passed on. 2026 Jan-Aug: HS 71 was 25.6% of imports from Russia in the four months Comtrade has (Jan-Mar, May; 12-44% by month), applied to the Jan-Aug total (refresh_2026.json) with an 18-33% range. Total imports and HS 71 come from the same Armstat data, so the remaining range is the +-3% customs margin plus 0-5% retained.

to_rus.reasoning: Belarus buys Russian crude at a Urals-linked netback (Urals quotation minus the Russian export duty, plus a small premium; Interfax 2020), not at Brent. The builder's Urals band reached Brent-like highs (1.92 in 2022). Netback index in EUR: Urals (MinFin annual averages 63.6, 41.7, 69.0, 76.1, 63.0, ~68, ~57.7 USD/bbl) minus the duty (about 13, 5.5, 8.6, 6.4, 2.6, 0, 0 USD/bbl as the tax manoeuvre phased it out) gives 1.20, 1.55, 1.31, 1.47, 1.20 (2021-2025); 2026 = builder Urals x 1.183 (no duty). Band -6%/+5% (2026 -8%/+8%) for the premium, the duty averaging and any discount. Gas is a fixed USD price, so its index is known to +-2%. The price width falls; the central index rises 2-6% (less volume bought), and the fuel windfall rises because the end of the export duty is counted as a price rise.
